objectives.text: Stay sovereign between two giants by spreading ties to third neighbours. The phrase is current: in Washington on 2 Aug 2023 PM Oyun-Erdene called the United States an 'important strategic third neighbor' and said that a landlocked Mongolia would suffer if great-power rivalry turned into a new Cold War. The same logic brings Japan, South Korea, the EU, India and Turkey into the picture, none of which can replace the two neighbours for trade or fuel.

constraints.text: The ICC is a legal constraint that has not bound: Mongolia is a State Party to the Rome Statute. Putin came to Ulaanbaatar on 3 Sept 2024 on the ICC warrant of March 2023 and was not arrested; the EU said Mongolia did not comply with its statute duty. The cost was a reputational one and the dependence on Russian fuel explains the choice (a Politico-quoted legal expert expected no sanction beyond a possible non-compliance finding; the ICC outcome was not found).

paradoxes.text: The third-neighbour policy is meant to escape single dependence, but the mining plan deepens it: the rail link to China is sold as the way to lift coal exports from 83 to 165 Mt a year, so the more Mongolia monetises its minerals the more its exports go to one buyer (about 91% already). The rail that answers the 'landlocked' problem also ties the export income to Beijing.

grand_strategy.reading:
Mongolia runs a strategy of buffering: a landlocked state between Russia and China
that sells its ground (coal, copper, gold) to one neighbour, buys its fuel from the other,
and calls the spread of other partners a third neighbour policy. The posture is neutral
in words and dependent in structure. The 2024 election gave the Mongolian People's Party
68 of 126 seats, a narrow majority after a supermajority, and the 2025 shift at the top
came from the street and from the house: Prime Minister Oyun-Erdene lost a confidence vote
on 3 June 2025 with 44 votes against the 64 needed, and parliament confirmed Zandanshatar
on 13 June. Later accounts disagree: Al Jazeera reports Zandanshatar losing a confidence
vote and resigning in October 2025, while Wikipedia's crisis summary says a presidential veto
and a court ruling kept him in office; a 2026 cabinet infobox records a dissolution in April
2026 with a successor. Current leadership is not confirmed here. The two dated acts that show
the strategy at work are the Putin visit of September 2024 (the ICC warrant unenforced
under fuel dependence) and the September 2025 PoS-2 memorandum (the transit fee as a bet, the
price still open). A non-event is a signal: Mongolia is not an observer of the Organization of
Turkic States (OTS observers page), although the OTS secretary-general visited Ulaanbaatar in
March 2025 at the Mongolian foreign minister's invitation. Gaps not closed here: the Mongolian
script question in detail, the Turkish and Kazakh bilateral figures, the India refinery (1.5 Mt,
Indian investment, construction pushed to 2028 per one commentary, tier 4), the EU beyond the
2017 agreement, and any US contact after 2023.

stances.note: Cooperation out of dependence, without alignment: no treaty of alliance is in our sources. Russia supplies about 95% of petroleum products (ministry figure, end 2025), and Mongolia signed a memorandum of intent with Gazprom in August 2025 and a legally binding memorandum on the Power of Siberia 2 transit route on 2 Sep 2025 (gas of 50 bcm a year for 30 years, price not agreed). Putin visited Ulaanbaatar on 3 Sep 2024 despite the ICC warrant, and Mongolia did not arrest him. Trend stable: the transit deal and the visit point up, the fuel dependence and the 2026 supply crisis point down. Since is the date of the latest dated move, not the start of the relation (not sourced). Bond - affinity, our reading: no shared identity claim, a Soviet-era protector and a neighbour with Buddhist and Buryat ties. Confidence B: one tier-1 ministry statement and tier-3 reporting.

stances.note: Transactional and structural: China takes about 91-92% of exports (91.9% in Jan-May 2025, 91.2% in Jan-Sep 2025, secondary summaries of customs and central-bank data; the NSO release was not retrieved), coal is about 46-48% and copper about 35-37% of exports in the same months. The Ganqimaodu-Gashuunsukhait rail link was signed and ratified on 14 Feb 2025 and track-laying began on 1 Sep 2025 (completion targeted 2027). Mongolia does not align with Beijing: there is no treaty of alliance in our sources, and the government's concern for its language and script is kept mostly in domestic policy. Grievance is the bond in the live wound of the 2020 Inner Mongolia Mandarin-schooling protests, which Mongolia watches for its own script and language. Confidence C: tier-3 and secondary figures only. The grade is partner not reluctant partner: no source in our set uses the word reluctant for this pair.

stances.note: The third neighbour in use: PM Oyun-Erdene met Vice President Harris at the White House on 2 Aug 2023 and called the US an important strategic third neighbour, with cooperation pledged on security, space and critical minerals including rare earths (an MoU of June 2023 between the mining ministry and the State Department). The Open Skies aviation agreement was signed on 4 Aug 2023, letting the national carrier MIAT fly direct to a US airport. Partner, not ally: the pledges are economic and transactional. No 2025 or 2026 US visit was found in the sources, so the warming rests on 2023 alone. Bond - none: pure interest. Confidence C: tier-3 reporting only.

stances.note: Aid and investment without alignment. Japan agreed in March 2025 to about 545 million yen in grant aid for air-pollution monitors and sewerage equipment, and gave the Mongolian army an air traffic control radar worth 1.3 billion yen as the first provision of its official security assistance programme. Warming is dated to 2025 by these grants; the relation predates them (relations since 24 Feb 1972 per the Mongolian foreign ministry list, date only). The Wikipedia index mentions aid of about 1.2 billion dollars over 1991-2003 and calls Japan a major ally, with no citation: not used as a grade. Bond - affinity: sympathy and aid, no kinship. Confidence C: one tier-3 report, plus the Wikipedia index (tier 4).

stances.note: Labour and investment, transactional. About 54,800 Mongolians lived in South Korea at the end of 2023, the 11th-largest foreign group (about 4,600 under the Employment Permit System, about 18,500 undocumented; the two totals in the same presentation differ by a thousand). A 2016 state visit agreed 14 projects worth about 4.49 billion USD (urban development, power, rail, transmission). A Korean supply deal for oil products is reported as signed (tier-4 commentary), the fuel diversification away from Russia being the new use of the tie. Relations since 26 Mar 1990 (Mongolian foreign ministry list, date only). Bond - none. Confidence C: older reporting and one 2024 presentation.
